questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential district if no sign is posted?
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in a residential district is 25 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that sign instead.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles cannot be seen 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, must drivers yield to cars that arrived before them?
questions.explanation: Yes. At a four-way stop, you must let drivers who arrived first go through first. Wait your turn.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What is the correct rule at a four-way stop?

options.text: Drivers can demand the right-of-way, even if it causes an accident.
The driver who arrives first should go through first.
Drivers can slow down and proceed if the road looks clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first should go through first.
questions.explanation: The driver who reaches the four-way stop first should go through the intersection first. Drivers proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If your car loses grip on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the same speed to get better grip.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road and ride on water (hydroplaning), slow down gradually and do not brake. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 miles per hour in heavy rain.

questions.question: Can you use parking lights instead of headlights at night?
questions.explanation: No. You must use headlights at night. Using only parking lights is against the law when visibility is low.

questions.question: When must headlights be used?
questions.explanation: Use headlights between sunset and sunrise. Also use them anytime visibility is reduced.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive in fog?

options.text: It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when visibility drops to 500 feet or less. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What is the penalty for using a handheld phone to read, type, or send messages while driving?

options.text: A secondary offense with a fine of $50 to $100
A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500

questions.correctAnswerText: A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500
questions.explanation: Using a handheld phone to read, type, or send messages while driving is a secondary offense. The fine is $200 to $500.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers need to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must also stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving at night, using only your parking lights is unlawful.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive at night using only your parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on the bottom. On a horizontal traffic signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests or bright jackets. They use paddles and red flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers may not be able to see you behind them. Increase your following distance. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with more force, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with more force, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, steering will be harder. Reduce your speed and pull off the roadway to a safe area to stop.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because you are less likely to see another vehicle coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep the pedestrian safe.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not go until all gates are raised and all warning signals have stopped flashing.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food can slow alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about laws they must follow. These signs may show traffic direction, lane use, turning rules, speed limits, parking rules, or other special situations. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: When can you proceed at a red traffic light with a green arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
After you wait for the light to change.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow signal, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.
